problem: PROP-7 (T3, required: true) claims V4 is verified via 'record-earn's anti-fake gate AND an independent browser/on-chain check,' and REQ-16 requires 'bank receipt for human-funded' verification per rail. Neither the behavioral spec nor the verification architecture defines HOW a bank receipt is independently checked in a zero-human way -- there is no bank API integration, no stated mechanism for reading a bank statement/note.com payout dashboard autonomously, and no discussion of the 2FA/login barrier such a check would hit. The design source itself explicitly names this as unresolved and hard: 'GATE 3 GET PAID (KYC) ★ the real wall ★ note/Substack/Zenn/X withdrawals need a BANK account + identity verification. This, not login, is the zero-human blocker.' The behavioral spec/verification architecture treat this as already solved by asserting it as a required T3 gate with no defined implementation path, and any naive implementation (e.g. logging into online banking to screenshot a balance) would itself require a human-assisted login/2FA step, directly re-violating REQ-2.
fix: Either (a) define the concrete zero-human bank-receipt verification mechanism (e.g. a specific bank/payment-processor API with stored credentials + programmatic 2FA bypass, matching the pattern already proven for Gmail-OTP) before marking PROP-7's human-funded leg as required:true, or (b) explicitly descope PROP-7's human-funded bank-receipt verification from Sprint 1/2 required gates and mark it an open risk, since as written it cannot be objectively verified without contradicting REQ-2.
